stem: Light year is a unit of
solution: A light year is the distance light travels in one year, so it is a unit of distance. Matches option C.

stem: Which of the following is not equal to watt?
solution: Power (watt) equals \(J/s\), and by \(P=VI=I^2R\) it also equals ampere-volt and \((\text{ampere})^2\)-ohm. Ampere/volt has the unit of \(1/\text{ohm}\) (conductance), not power. Matches option D.

stem: Newton-second is the unit of
solution: Impulse \(=F\,\Delta t\) has the unit newton-second and equals the change in momentum, so newton-second is the unit of momentum. Matches option C.

stem: Which of the following is not represented in the correct unit?
solution: Stress/strain (Young's modulus) is \(N/m^2\), surface tension is \(N/m\), and pressure is \(N/m^2\) — all correct. Energy must be \(kg\,m^2/s^2\) (joule); \(kg\text{-}m/sec\) is momentum, not energy. Matches option C.

stem: One nanometre is equal to
solution: \(1\ nm = 10^{-9}\ m = 10^{-9}\times 100\ cm = 10^{-7}\ cm\). Matches option C.

stem: Which of the following is not a unit of energy?
solution: Watt-second (\(=J\)), newton-metre (\(=J\)) and joule are all units of energy. \(kg\,m/sec\) is momentum, not energy. Matches option B.

stem: In \(S=a+bt+ct^2\), \(S\) is measured in metres and \(t\) in seconds. The unit of \(c\) is
solution: Every term must have the unit of \(S\) (metre). \(ct^2\) is in metres, so \(c\) has the unit \(m/s^2 = ms^{-2}\). Matches option D.

stem: Joule-second is the unit of
solution: Joule-second is the unit of angular momentum (and of Planck's constant), since \(L=I\omega\) has the unit \(J\,s\). Matches option D.

stem: Wavelength of a ray of light is \(0.00006\ m\). It is equal to
solution: \(0.00006\ m = 6\times10^{-5}\ m\). One micron \(=10^{-6}\ m\), so \(6\times10^{-5}\ m = 60\times10^{-6}\ m = 60\) microns. Matches option B.

stem: Density of wood is \(0.5\ gm/cc\) in the CGS system of units. The corresponding value in MKS units is
solution: \(1\ g/cm^3 = 1000\ kg/m^3\), so \(0.5\ g/cm^3 = 500\ kg/m^3\). Matches option A.

stem: One Mach number is equal to
solution: Mach number is the ratio of speed to the speed of sound; Mach 1 equals the speed of sound, about \(332\ m/s\). Matches option B.

stem: Volt/metre is the unit of
solution: Electric field intensity \(E=V/d\) has the unit volt per metre. Matches option D.

stem: If the unit of length and force be increased four times, then the unit of energy is
solution: Energy \(=\) force \(\times\) length. If both units increase 4 times, the energy unit increases \(4\times4=16\) times. Matches option C.

stem: If \(u_1\) and \(u_2\) are the units selected in two systems of measurement and \(n_1\) and \(n_2\) their numerical values, then
solution: The physical quantity is fixed, so numerical value times unit is invariant: \(n_1 u_1 = n_2 u_2\). Matches option A.

stem: To determine the Young's modulus of a wire, the formula is \(Y=\dfrac{F}{A}\cdot\dfrac{L}{\Delta L}\), where \(L\) = length, \(A\) = area of cross-section, and \(\Delta L\) = change in length under a force \(F\). The conversion factor to change it from CGS to MKS system is
solution: \(Y\) has the dimensions of pressure, \(ML^{-1}T^{-2}\). Converting CGS to MKS: \(\dfrac{n_2}{n_1}=\dfrac{M_1}{M_2}\left(\dfrac{L_1}{L_2}\right)^{-1}=10^{-3}\times(10^{-2})^{-1}=0.1\). Matches option C.

stem: The equation \(\left(P+\dfrac{a}{V^2}\right)(V-b)=\) constant. The units of \(a\) are
solution: \(a/V^2\) must have the unit of pressure, so \(a=P\,V^2\). In CGS, \(P\) is \(dyne/cm^2\) and \(V^2\) is \((cm^3)^2=cm^6\), giving \(a=(dyne/cm^2)(cm^6)=dyne\,cm^4\). Matches option B.

stem: In the C.G.S. system the magnitude of a force is 100 dynes. In another system where the fundamental physical quantities are kilogram, metre and minute, the magnitude of the force is
solution: Force has the dimensions \(MLT^{-2}\). \(n_2=n_1\dfrac{M_1}{M_2}\dfrac{L_1}{L_2}\left(\dfrac{T_1}{T_2}\right)^{-2}=100\times10^{-3}\times10^{-2}\times60^2=100\times10^{-5}\times3600=3.6\). Matches option C.

stem: Dimensional formula \(ML^2T^{-3}\) represents
solution: Power \(=\) energy/time \(=\dfrac{ML^2T^{-2}}{T}=ML^2T^{-3}\). Matches option B.

stem: If \(L\) and \(R\) are respectively the inductance and resistance, then the dimensions of \(\dfrac{L}{R}\) will be
optD: Cannot be represented in terms of \(M, L\) and \(T\)
solution: \(L/R\) is the inductive time constant, which has the dimension of time. Answer keyed to the official LWS key (option B).
reviewNote: Physics note: \(L/R\) has the dimension of time \(M^0 L^0 T\) (option C); the LWS key marks option B \(M^0 L T^1\). Keyed to the LWS key per instruction — the official key appears to be in error here.

stem: Dimensional formula for latent heat is
solution: Latent heat \(=\) heat/mass \(=\dfrac{ML^2T^{-2}}{M}=M^0L^2T^{-2}\). Matches option A.

stem: The dimensional formula for Planck's constant \((h)\) is
solution: From \(E=h\nu\), \(h=E/\nu=\dfrac{ML^2T^{-2}}{T^{-1}}=ML^2T^{-1}\). Matches option C.

stem: The frequency of vibration \(f\) of a mass \(m\) suspended from a spring of spring constant \(K\) is \(f=C\,m^x K^y\), where \(C\) is a dimensionless quantity. The values of \(x\) and \(y\) are
solution: \(f=\dfrac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\dfrac{K}{m}}\), so \(f\propto m^{-1/2}K^{1/2}\), giving \(x=-\tfrac12,\ y=\tfrac12\). Matches option D.

stem: The quantities \(A\) and \(B\) are related by \(m=A/B\), where \(m\) is the linear density and \(A\) is the force. The dimensions of \(B\) are of
solution: Linear density \(m=ML^{-1}\) and force \(A=MLT^{-2}\). \(B=A/m=\dfrac{MLT^{-2}}{ML^{-1}}=L^2T^{-2}=M^0L^2T^{-2}\), the dimensions of latent heat. Matches option C.

stem: The velocity of water waves \(v\) may depend upon their wavelength \(\lambda\), the density of water \(\rho\) and the acceleration due to gravity \(g\). The method of dimensions gives the relation
solution: Writing \(v\propto\lambda^a\rho^b g^c\) and matching dimensions: \(M\Rightarrow b=0\); \(T\Rightarrow c=\tfrac12\); \(L\Rightarrow a=\tfrac12\). Hence \(v\propto\sqrt{\lambda g}\), i.e. \(v^2\propto g\lambda\). Matches option C.

stem: The equation of a wave is \(Y=A\sin\omega\left(\dfrac{x}{v}-k\right)\), where \(\omega\) is the angular velocity and \(v\) is the linear velocity. The dimension of \(k\) is
solution: The argument of the sine is dimensionless. \(\omega\,\dfrac{x}{v}\) is dimensionless, so \(\omega k\) must also be dimensionless, giving \(k=1/\omega=T\). Matches option B.

stem: A force vector applied on a mass is \(\vec{F}=6\hat{i}-8\hat{j}+10\hat{k}\) and it accelerates the body at \(1\ m/s^2\). What is the mass of the body (in kg)?
solution: \(|\vec F|=\sqrt{6^2+8^2+10^2}=\sqrt{200}=10\sqrt2\) N. With \(a=1\ m/s^2\), \(m=|\vec F|/a=10\sqrt2\) kg. Matches option A.

subtopic: Dot Product, Cross Product and Angle
stem: Two adjacent sides of a parallelogram are represented by \(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\) and \(3\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+\hat{k}\). What is the area of the parallelogram?
solution: Area \(=|\vec A\times\vec B|\). \(\vec A\times\vec B=8\hat i+8\hat j-8\hat k\), so area \(=\sqrt{8^2+8^2+8^2}=\sqrt{192}=8\sqrt3\). Matches option B.

subtopic: Dot Product, Cross Product and Angle
stem: The position vector of the radius is given by the vectors \(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}\) and \(2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+\hat{k}\), while the linear momentum is \(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-\hat{k}\). Then the angular momentum is
solution: Taking the radius vector as \(\vec r=(2\hat i-3\hat j+\hat k)-(2\hat i+\hat j+\hat k)=-4\hat j\) and \(\vec p=2\hat i+3\hat j-\hat k\), the angular momentum \(\vec L=\vec r\times\vec p=4\hat i+8\hat k\). The component magnitudes match option B (printed key taken as B).
reviewNote: Flawed / ambiguous: derivation gives \(4\hat i+8\hat k\); the closest printed option B is \(4\hat i-8\hat k\) (the \(\hat k\) sign differs), so the exact result is not among the printed options. Verify against the LWS answer key.

subtopic: Dot Product, Cross Product and Angle
stem: What is the value of linear velocity if \(\vec{\omega}=3\hat{i}-4\hat{j}+\hat{k}\) and \(\vec{r}=5\hat{i}-6\hat{j}+6\hat{k}\)?
solution: \(\vec v=\vec\omega\times\vec r\). Evaluating the determinant gives \(\vec v=-18\hat i-13\hat j+2\hat k\). Matches option D.

subtopic: Dot Product, Cross Product and Angle
stem: A force \(\vec{F}=(5\hat{i}+3\hat{j})\) N is applied on a particle which displaces it to \(\vec{s}=(2\hat{i}-\hat{j})\) m. The work done on the particle is
solution: Work \(=\vec F\cdot\vec s=(5)(2)+(3)(-1)=10-3=7\) J. Matches option B.

subtopic: Dot Product, Cross Product and Angle
stem: If a vector \(\vec{A}\) is parallel to another vector \(\vec{B}\), then the resultant of \(\vec{A}\times\vec{B}\) will be equal to
solution: For parallel vectors the angle is \(0\), so \(|\vec A\times\vec B|=AB\sin 0=0\); the cross product is the zero vector. Matches option C.

stem: A moves with 65 km/h while B is coming from behind A with 80 km/h. The relative velocity of B with respect to A is
solution: 'B is coming back of A' is read as B moving toward A in the opposite direction, so the relative velocity of B with respect to A is \(80+65=145\) km/h. Matches option D.
reviewNote: Wording ambiguous: opposite-direction reading gives 145 km/h (option D, per the LWS key); a same-direction reading (B behind, catching up) would give 15 km/h (option C).

stem: A thief is running away on a jeep moving at 9 m/s. A policeman chases him on a motorcycle moving at 10 m/s. If the instantaneous separation of the jeep from the motorcycle is 100 m, how long will it take the policeman to catch the thief?
solution: The closing speed is \(10-9=1\ m/s\), so time \(=100/1=100\) s. Matches option D.

stem: A boat takes two hours to travel 8 km and back in still water. If the velocity of water is 4 km/h, the time taken for going 8 km upstream and coming back is
optD: Cannot be estimated with the information given
solution: In still water 16 km in 2 h gives a boat speed of 8 km/h. Upstream speed \(=8-4=4\) km/h (2 h for 8 km); downstream \(=8+4=12\) km/h (\(8/12\) h \(=40\) min). Total \(=2\) h 40 min. Matches option B.

stem: Two equal forces have their resultant equal to either of the forces. At what angle are they inclined?
solution: \(R^2=F^2+F^2+2F^2\cos\theta=F^2\) gives \(\cos\theta=-\tfrac12\), so \(\theta=120^\circ\). Matches option A.

stem: A unit vector parallel to the resultant of the vectors \(\vec{A}=4\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+6\hat{k}\) and \(\vec{B}=-\hat{i}+8\hat{j}-8\hat{k}\) is
solution: \(\vec A+\vec B=3\hat i+11\hat j-2\hat k\), and \(|\vec A+\vec B|=\sqrt{9+121+4}=\sqrt{134}\). The unit vector is \(\dfrac{3\hat i+11\hat j-2\hat k}{\sqrt{134}}\). Matches option C.

stem: Two equal forces act at a point and are inclined to each other at an angle of \(60^\circ\). The magnitude of their resultant is
solution: \(R=\sqrt{A^2+A^2+2A^2\cos 60^\circ}=\sqrt{3A^2}=\sqrt3\,A\). Matches option A.

subtopic: Dot Product, Cross Product and Angle
stem: Two vectors \(\vec{A}\) and \(\vec{B}\) are such that \(|\vec{A}+\vec{B}|=|\vec{A}-\vec{B}|\). Then the angle between the two vectors \(\vec{A}\) and \(\vec{B}\) will be
solution: Squaring, \(|\vec A+\vec B|^2=|\vec A-\vec B|^2\) gives \(4\,\vec A\cdot\vec B=0\), so the angle is \(90^\circ=\pi/2\). Matches option D.

stem: The vector projection of a vector \(3\hat{i}+5\hat{k}\) on the y-axis is
solution: The vector has no \(\hat j\) component, so its projection on the y-axis is zero. Matches option D.

subtopic: Dot Product, Cross Product and Angle
stem: If \(|\vec{A}\times\vec{B}|=\dfrac{\vec{A}\cdot\vec{B}}{\sqrt{3}}\), then the value of the angle between \(\vec{A}\) and \(\vec{B}\) is
solution: \(AB\sin\theta=\dfrac{AB\cos\theta}{\sqrt3}\) gives \(\tan\theta=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}\), so \(\theta=30^\circ=\pi/6\). Matches option D.

subtopic: Dot Product, Cross Product and Angle
stem: If a vector \(2\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+6\hat{k}\) is perpendicular to the vector \(5\hat{i}+6\hat{j}-a\hat{k}\), then the value of \(a\) is
solution: Perpendicular means the dot product is zero: \((2)(5)+(4)(6)+(6)(-a)=0\Rightarrow 34-6a=0\Rightarrow a=\dfrac{17}{3}\). Matches option D.

subtopic: Dot Product, Cross Product and Angle
stem: Consider two vectors \(\vec{F}_1=2\hat{i}+5\hat{k}\) and \(\vec{F}_2=3\hat{j}+4\hat{k}\). The magnitude of the scalar product of these vectors is
solution: \(\vec F_1\cdot\vec F_2=(2)(0)+(0)(3)+(5)(4)=20\). Matches option D.

subtopic: Dot Product, Cross Product and Angle
stem: What is the angle between \(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}\) and \(\hat{i}\)?
solution: \(\cos\theta=\dfrac{(\hat i+\hat j+\hat k)\cdot\hat i}{\sqrt3\cdot 1}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}\), so \(\theta=\cos^{-1}\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}\approx 54.7^\circ\), which is none of \(\pi/6,\ \pi/4,\ \pi/2\). Matches option D.

stem: A boy walks 10 m towards east, then turns left and moves 5 m straight on the ground. He then climbs 15 m via a ladder onto the roof of the house. What is his displacement vector with respect to the starting point?
solution: Taking east as \(\hat i\), north as \(\hat j\) and vertical as \(\hat k\): 10 m east, then left is north (5 m), then 15 m up gives \(10\hat i+5\hat j+15\hat k\). Matches option A.

stem: The vector joining the points \(A(1,1,-1)\) and \(B(2,-3,4)\) and pointing from A to B is
solution: \(\vec{AB}=B-A=(2-1)\hat i+(-3-1)\hat j+(4+1)\hat k=\hat i-4\hat j+5\hat k\). Matches option C.

stem: A hall has the dimensions \(10\ m \times 12\ m \times 14\ m\). A fly, starting at one corner, ends up at the diametrically opposite corner. The magnitude of its displacement is nearly
solution: The body diagonal \(=\sqrt{10^2+12^2+14^2}=\sqrt{100+144+196}=\sqrt{440}\approx 21\) m. Matches option D.

stem: A particle is moving westward with a velocity \(\vec{v}_1=5\ m/s\). Its velocity changes to \(\vec{v}_2=5\ m/s\) northward. The change in velocity vector \(\left(\Delta\vec{V}=\vec{v}_2-\vec{v}_1\right)\) is
solution: \(\Delta\vec V=\vec v_2-\vec v_1\) has magnitude \(5\sqrt2\) m/s. Answer keyed to the official LWS key (option D).
reviewNote: Physics note: for the printed stem ('westward' then northward), \(\Delta\vec V=\vec v_2-\vec v_1\) points north-east (option A); the LWS key marks option D (north-west), which is the answer to the 'eastward then northward' variant. Keyed to the LWS key per instruction — the printed stem likely should read 'eastward'.

stem: Six vectors \(\vec{a}\) through \(\vec{f}\) have the magnitudes and directions indicated in the figure: \(\vec{a}\) points east, \(\vec{b}\) points down, \(\vec{c}\) points east, \(\vec{d}\) points up, \(\vec{e}\) points west, and \(\vec{f}\) points up-and-to-the-left. Which of the following statements is true?
solution: \(\vec d\) points up and \(\vec e\) points west; their sum points up-and-to-the-left, which is the direction of \(\vec f\). Matches option D.
reviewNote: The stem embeds a figure (six arrows a-f); the directions are described in words here for the OMR sheet. Answer keyed from the figure directions.

stem: A particle goes from point \(A(3,2,1)\) to point \(B(4,3,2)\). Find the unit vector along \(\vec{AB}\).
solution: \(\vec{AB}=\hat i+\hat j+\hat k\) and \(|\vec{AB}|=\sqrt3\). The unit vector is \(\dfrac{\hat i+\hat j+\hat k}{\sqrt3}\). Matches option C.

subtopic: Dot Product, Cross Product and Angle
stem: If \(\vec{A}=3\hat{i}+4\hat{j}\) and \(\vec{B}=a\hat{i}+3\hat{j}\) are perpendicular to each other, the value of \(a\) is
solution: Perpendicular means \(\vec A\cdot\vec B=0\): \(3a+12=0\Rightarrow a=-4\). Matches option A.
